key_insight: Dense 3D tracking can build on strong pretrained 2D trackers and 3D geometry models instead of learning everything jointly. Even lifting 2D tracks into 3D and interpolating occluded segments can rival dedicated 3D trackers.
problem_solved: Tracking points through monocular video requires matching them across frames, estimating depth, and recovering motion during occlusion—all with limited 4D training supervision.
method: Use a pretrained 2D tracker to establish point correspondences across video frames.
Lift those tracks into 3D using estimates from a pretrained geometry model.
Frame tracking as lifted trajectory repair; the provided abstract highlights simple interpolation across occluded segments as a strong baseline.
impact: Reusing pretrained tracking and geometry models offers a practical foundation for dense 3D tracking without learning every component jointly. The findings highlight the importance of strong modular baselines when evaluating specialized tracking systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: monocular video → 2D tracks + 3D geometry → lifted 3D trajectories.
Video frames with colored point tracks, including an object passing behind an occluder.
3D trajectory plot with solid observed segments and dashed interpolated gaps.
Side-by-side schematic contrasting joint end-to-end learning with pretrained modular components.
paper_title: ReLift: Dense 3D Tracking as Lifted Trajectory Repair
paper_authors: Assaf Singer, Maroun Khriesh, Noam Rotstein, Yoni Kasten, Or Litany
